title: Embed rerank debug scratchpad - dim mismatch & latency
content:
TL;DR
Quick personal notes while chasing a couple of anomalies on embeddings + rerank endpoints: intermittent dimension mismatch errors (expected 1536, got 1024) and correlated latency spikes on P95/P99 during bursts. Repro steps, commands I ran, snippets from logs, hypotheses, and next actions below. Mostly a scratchpad — messy.

Summary of incidents (observed in last 48h)
- Incident A (2024-11-11 09:10 UTC): several API clients reported 400s with 'DimensionMismatchError: expected 1536 got 1024' when hitting /v1/rerank.
- Incident B (2024-11-11 09:10-09:30 UTC): same timeframe saw P95 latency for rerank jump from ~220ms -> ~1.8s on the hosted tier. Correlated drop in throughput (backpressure).
- Clients using hosted embeddings endpoint reported that their embeddings length suddenly became 1024 for a subset of requests. Not all customers.

Repro attempt notes (local and prod)
1) Reproduce simple roundtrip locally (python). Some requests succeed, some fail — non-deterministic when concurrent threads are used.
Commands run:
- curl to embeddings endpoint:
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference/v1/embeddings \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n    -d '{"model":"open-mosaic-embedding-large","input":"test sentence"}' | jq '.data[0].embedding | length'
  -> returns 1536 normally, but intermittently returns 1024 in the wild.

- Local python stress test (threads = 50):
  python - <<PY
import requests,threading
def f():
  r = requests.post('https://api.redwood-inference/v1/embeddings', json={'model':'open-mosaic-embedding-large','input':'x'*20}, headers={'Authorization':'Bearer %s'%'REDACT'})
  print(r.status_code, len(r.json().get('data',[{}])[0].get('embedding',[])))
threads=[threading.Thread(target=f) for _ in range(50)]
[t.start() for t in threads]
[t.join() for t in threads]
PY
  -> locally I could not reproduce 1024 consistently; only reproduced when hitting staging with lower capacity and scaled-down worker count.

2) Rerank request that triggers mismatch (sample):
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference/v1/rerank \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n    -d '{"model":"rerank-small","queries":["q1"],"candidates":[{"id":"a","emb": [0.1, ...]}, {"id":"b","emb": [0.2, ...]}]}'
  -> server returns 400 + message: "DimensionMismatchError: expected 1536 got 1024" and trace: \"serving_runtime.embedding.validate:dim_check failed for candidate[1]\"

Observed logs (snippets copied from prod span logs)
- 2024-11-11T09:12:07Z [rerank-worker-3] WARN InputValidation: candidate_emb_dim != model_emb_dim (1024 != 1536) request_id=req-xfb2
- 2024-11-11T09:12:08Z [emb-service-7] INFO model-switch: pin=open-mosaic-embedding-large -> unpinned, fallback=open-mosaic-embedding-medium request_id=req-xfa9
- 2024-11-11T09:12:09Z [routing] ERROR grpc deadline exceeded (client=svc-proxy) request_id=req-xfb3
- 2024-11-11T09:13:01Z [autoscaler] DEBUG scale-down: candidate nodes to retire=2 due to cpu overcommit request_id=req-xfc0

Metric snapshots (from console, times aligned)
- 09:10 UTC
  rerank p50: 120ms, p95: 220ms, p99: 340ms, qps: 48
- 09:12 UTC (spike)
  rerank p50: 210ms, p95: 1.8s, p99: 3.2s, qps: 160 (burst, queued requests)
- embeddings service error rate: 0.3% -> 4.2% during 09:10-09:18

Quick hypothesis list (ordered by my prior)
1) Client mix: some clients still calling old-embedding model variant that produces 1024-dim vectors while the rerank model expects 1536. This could be because of routing (smart routing sent them to older model variant).
2) Unpinned model rollout/rollback: logs show 'unpinned' events for open-mosaic-embedding-large — maybe a deployment/rollback caused a fallback to a medium variant (1024) under load.
3) Cache/binary serialization bug: embedding cache or prefix cache storing vectors without shape metadata, and when reloading from cache the shape metadata is dropped (or overridden) causing consumers to believe it's 1536 when actually 1024.
4) Quantization fallback: a quantized runtime fallback path returns truncated embeddings shape (bug in kernel selection). Unlikely but plausible after recent runtime refactor.
5) Index mismatch: rerank service reading from an older index that was built from 1024-dim embeddings but the model was upgraded to 1536; if index vector dims mismatch, client-side validation will throw.
6) Backpressure/autoscaler flakiness: during burst autoscaler removed nodes -> some requests forced to fallback model variant (cheaper) to maintain latency, producing mixed dims.

What I tried (and results)
- Forced pin of open-mosaic-embedding-large on a small test org: errors stopped for that org. (=> supports hypothesis #2)
- Rebuilt rerank index from scratch using current embeddings: no mismatch locally.
- Replayed failing request IDs (from logs) against a pinned cluster: returned expected 1536 embeddings.
- Reviewed rollout PRs (see linked PR) — there was a config change to routing policy that allowed 'compatible-dim: true' to route across variants; flagged as suspicious.
- Disabled the 'compatible-dim' routing flag in staging; ran 1M requests over 30 mins — no dimension mismatches seen.

Actionable next steps (short list)
- Immediate: pin open-mosaic-embedding-large for the affected tenants and revert the routing 'compatible-dim' flag rollout. (Ops ticket: JIRA-INFR-88)
- Short-term: add stricter validation and telemetry when a rerank request sees mixed dims (emit vector_unexpected_dim metric with model_variant tag).
- Medium-term: ensure embedding objects carry explicit "dim" in metadata at payload and cache level; make cached entries schema-checked on load.
- Longer-term: add canary tests that simulate burst QPS and assert that model variant routing does not mix dims for dependent endpoints (rerank/indexing pipelines).

Notes / oddities to keep in mind
- Not every customer hit this. Likely because some customers pinned models or their traffic landed on different regions where rollout hadn't occurred.
- There were several autoscaler events right when the errors started — need to check if autoscaler policy allowed too-aggressive scale-down.
- There is an existing TODO in serving-runtime: "preserve-embedding-meta-on-cache-serialize" (PR referenced above) — might be related.

Quick checks I still want to run (later)
- Dump router decisions at request level (region, tier, model_variant) for a span that includes failing requests.
- Re-run the same stress test but with different client ids to see if user-level pinning affects behavior.
- Confirm whether quantized-variant kernels were involved. Check binary names in runtime logs (e.g., kernel=q8_0_1536 vs q4_0_1024).

Breadcrumbs for follow-ups (to copy into ticket)
- Example failing request-id: req-xfb2 (09:12:07Z)
- Example trace: span trace-url: https://traces.redwood/internal/trace/aa12b
- Suspect config change: routing "compatible-dim" enabled in PR #742 (see linked_artifacts)

If this turns into a persistent problem: could add a compatibility layer that auto-promotes 1024->1536 by zero-pad or learned projection but that's a hack and will hide root cause. Prefer to fix routing/pinning or cache metadata.

End of scratchpad — will copy bits into JIRA-INFR-88 and ping @ops and @applied-ml on Slack after pinning.
